request.spec:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
On the sheet a transfer brought a person to, a steward can undo it on the same sheet-today they
arrived (a button on the row; any later day, anyone else, or a person who did not arrive by transfer
is refused with an error on the row): the person is transferred back to the sheet they came from by
exactly the transfer rules and lines, and this sheet then writes PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name>
to=<sheet id>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Transfer undo is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests (the main "transfer undo" test plus scenarios 1–3).

**What it does:** on the sheet a person was transferred to, their row now has an "Undo transfer" button (`person-transfer-undo`). It only goes through when three things hold:
- the person arrived by transfer;
- the user pressing it is the steward who made that transfer;
- the sheet's today is still the day they arrived.

Otherwise it's refused, the error shows on the row (`person-error`), and nothing is changed or written to the audit file. When it goes through, the person is sent back to the sheet they came from by calling the existing transfer code, so the same rules, refusals and audit lines apply. This sheet then writes `PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE name=<name> to=<sheet id>`, followed by a `TOTALS` line when the totals moved, which is the order the test expects.

**Changes:**
- **Stored data:** migration `V95__person_arrival.sql` adds `arrived_on` (the sheet's today when the person arrived) and `arrived_by` (who transferred them) to `person`. A transfer now fills both in.
- **Server:** `PersonTransferService.undo` does the checks and the transfer back. The new endpoint is `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{id}/transfer-undo` in `PersonController`, and it also saves the state of the sheet the person went back to, as transfer already does for its target sheet.
- **Front end:** the button and its error handling are in `people.ts`. The button only appears for people who came from another sheet.

**Worth knowing:**
- People transferred before this change have no arrival record, so their transfers can't be undone.
- Someone transferred back by an undo counts as having arrived by transfer on their original sheet. The same steward could therefore undo the undo on that sheet the same day.
